solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Faff about with mike, interrupting popular singer

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of another, so the mike letter goes inside the singer

parts.note: Michael Bublé, the Canadian crooner, written without the accent
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone fusses around with a microphone, cutting in on a famous crooner's performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer is Michael Bublé; M sits inside his name after BU.
explanation.definitionFit: To bumble is to potter about ineffectually, which is what faffing about means in British slang.

clue.text: Report new work's in for keen reader

indicators.note: is in means placed inside the report word

parts.note: a boom is a loud report, like the bang of a gun

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the word's letters

explanation.surface: A notice says a new work has arrived for an enthusiastic reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' is a bang, not a document. 'new' rearranges the fodder to KWOR, and ''s in' sets it inside the bang word before its final M.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookworm is a person devoted to reading, an avid reader.

clue.text: Had good intentions but ultimately below average with skill

indicators.note: in a down clue, below places the next part after the earlier one

parts.note: the mean is the mathematical average

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: doing something well means doing it with skill

explanation.surface: Someone meant well but turned out to be below average in ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below average' looks like a single phrase; in fact the last letter of 'but' sits below MEAN in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To have meant well is to have had kind intentions, usually when the result disappointed.

clue.text: Longer opening more difficult in East End food store

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
Cockneys of London's East End are said to drop their aitches, so the H goes

parts.note: harder means more difficult

explanation.surface: A longer opening makes it more difficult to get into a food shop in the East End of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditionally working-class area of London where the Cockney accent drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool room or cupboard for keeping food, a pantry.

clue.text: Impeccable Selby beginning to sink fewer balls?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here taken from the snooker player's name

parts.note: in snooker, to sink a ball is to pot it, so sinking fewer balls is to 'pot less'

explanation.surface: A snooker commentator wonders whether flawless play by Mark Selby means potting fewer balls.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Selby is an English snooker champion; 'pot less' is read as a phrase, then joined to his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means without any blemish or fault, a close synonym of impeccable.

clue.text: Detective in charge cutting staff if force is reorganised

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into the staff word, so IC goes inside it

parts.note: a pole is a staff or rod

indicators.note: reorganised means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A detective in charge is cutting staff numbers while the police force is restructured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is reorganised' rearranges IF FORCE into OFFICER.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective is a kind of police officer, one who investigates crimes, so this is definition by example.

clue.text: Very good thing to have on pizza?

definitions.meaning: something spread on top of a pizza, such as cheese; the question mark flags the playful definition

explanation.definitionFit: Topping means excellent in old-fashioned British slang, and also an ingredient layered on a dish.

clue.text: World weariness that is mounting over news you heard

indicators.note: over means covering, so the reversed letters go around the rest
in a down clue, mounting means going up, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: N is new, so news, read as plural, gives two Ns

indicators.note: heard means the word is said aloud and spelt as the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Fatigue with the world grows as the news keeps coming to you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns the abbreviation upside down to EI in this down clue, and 'over' wraps it round the rest; 'heard' gives the letter that sounds like 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a listless boredom or weariness with life in general.

clue.text: Discover former partner has place on the South Coast

parts.note: to suss something out is to discover it, in British slang
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that their ex owns a home by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is a county on England's south coast, home to Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Sussex is an English county bordering the Channel, so it is an example of a south-coast place.

clue.text: Rude Croatian act's cut for broadcasting

indicators.note: rude in the sense of crude or rough-hewn, so the letters of the next word are roughly reworked
is cut means some letters are removed from the jumbled word, namely those of the following word

explanation.surface: A crude act by a Croatian performer has been edited out of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rude' scrambles CROATIAN and ''s cut' takes the letters A, C, T out of it, leaving the five letters rearranged as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is on air is being transmitted, i.e. broadcasting at that moment.

clue.text: Jack needs a drink with nose running after hot peppers

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
to lap is to drink as a cat does, tongue first

indicators.note: a running nose suggests something flowing out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jack wants a drink because his nose is streaming after eating chillies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges NOSE to ENOS, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jalapeños are a variety of Mexican chilli pepper with real heat.

clue.text: Good man, on time, repairing kit etc is exactly what's needed!

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the man word joins the time letter

parts.note: just means righteous, good
he is a man, by pronoun

indicators.note: repairing means putting the letters back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A decent fellow arrives on time to fix the kit and so forth, which is just what's wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repairing' rearranges KIT ETC into TICKET.
explanation.definitionFit: Just the ticket is an idiom for precisely the right thing for the situation.

clue.text: Women's group posted about Sodha's leader in Observer

parts.note: the WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for posted reads backwards

parts.note: posted a letter means sent it

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A women's group circulated a report about Sodha, a figure who led a piece in the Observer newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday paper and Sodha one of its columnists, but here observer just means onlooker. 'about' turns SENT into TNES.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness is someone who sees an event happen, an onlooker or observer.

clue.text: Prompt to describe one's current cooking style

indicators.note: to describe can mean to draw a line round, so the prompt word encloses the others

parts.note: a cue is a prompt given to an actor
one is I, plus the 's, for one is
in means fashionable, current

explanation.surface: A request for a description of today's way of cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to describe' is used in its geometrical sense of drawing a line around something, so the prompt word encloses the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuisine is a characteristic manner of preparing food, such as French or Thai cooking.

clue.text: Kedgeree known to possess a strong smell

indicators.note: the two words together possess, or contain, the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Kedgeree, the smoked fish and rice dish, is famous for its pungent odour.
explanation.walkthrough: Kedgeree is a British breakfast dish of smoked fish, rice and egg; the answer spans the end of it and the start of 'known'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reek as a noun is a powerful unpleasant odour, a stench.

clue.text: Mightily in error heading off to follow holy woman

indicators.note: the next part is placed after the saint abbreviation

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a holy man or woman

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word is removed

parts.note: wrongly means in error

explanation.surface: A holy woman is mightily mistaken when she goes the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' strips the W from WRONGLY to leave RONGLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Strongly and mightily are both adverbs for acting with great force or power.

clue.text: Finally finish old cub hut refit to hold large group of kids

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter
to hold means to contain, so the rearranged letters enclose L
a refit rebuilds something, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: At last the old Cub Scout hut is to be refurbished to accommodate a big gang of children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally finish' reads as one instruction, but 'finish' takes the end of 'Finally'. 'refit' turns CUB HUT into UTHCUB, which holds L.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth club is an organised gathering of young people for leisure activities.

clue.text: Soldiers make home in colony

parts.note: soldier ants are a caste of ants, so soldiers can mean ants
to nest is to make a home

explanation.surface: Troops settle within a colonial territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' and 'colony' suggest an empire; both belong to the insect world here.
explanation.definitionFit: An ants' nest houses a colony of ants, so the colony stands for its home.

clue.text: Stop! Holiday's cancelled

parts.note: leave is time off work, a holiday
an event that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry on hearing that a vacation has been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave off is an informal imperative telling someone to cease doing something.

clue.text: Conform with modern times to fit in

indicators.note: in tells us the word for fit goes inside the other two pieces joined together

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the modern era of dates
apt means fit or suitable

explanation.surface: To fit in, someone must conform with the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt to something is to adjust oneself to suit it, i.e. to comply or conform.

clue.text: One in five question tax return

indicators.note: return means the letters come back in reverse order

parts.note: NI is National Insurance, a British payroll tax

explanation.surface: A query about a tax return, apparently one of five forms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax return' looks like the form, but 'return' reverses NI, the UK's National Insurance contribution.
explanation.definitionFit: A quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born at a single birth.

clue.text: Top level coach keeps account with an old-fashioned calculator

parts.note: A is the top grade, first class

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the coach word contains the account letters

parts.note: a coach is a long-distance bus

explanation.surface: A top coach keeps the score using an outdated adding device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' is a vehicle, not a trainer: BUS keeps AC.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads on rods used for counting since ancient times.

clue.text: Unknown prey scattered and hard to intercept in wind

parts.note: Z is an unknown quantity in algebra

indicators.note: to intercept is to come between, so H goes into the jumbled letters
scattered means spread about, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Prey animals disperse, hard to catch in a strong wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges PREY to EPYR, and H cuts in to give EPHYR.
explanation.definitionFit: A zephyr is a gentle breeze, named after Zephyrus, the Greek god of the west wind.

clue.text: Bit stressed when Mum's involved making rice

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up within, so these letters go inside
stressed suggests being bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
Ma is a word for mum; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone gets a bit stressed when their mother gets involved in the cooking of rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stressed' rearranges the first word to B..TI, and 'involved' places the other two pieces between its first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati is a long-grain aromatic rice grown in India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Little bit of a brawl

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a fight

explanation.definitionFit: Scrap means both a small leftover piece and, colloquially, a scuffle or fistfight.

clue.text: Credit energies church put into opening of Sunday nurseries

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: the church abbreviation is placed between the two energy letters

parts.note: E stands for energy in physics, so two energies give two Es

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A church channels credit and energy into launching Sunday childcare.
explanation.definitionFit: A crèche is a day nursery where young children are minded while parents work or attend services.

clue.text: Building manager has job keeping track every now and then

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the picked letters go within

parts.note: a career is one's job or profession

indicators.note: taking a letter every now and then means alternate letters

explanation.surface: A building manager's job includes keeping track of things from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every now and then' takes the first, third and fifth letters of 'track', giving TAK; 'keeping' puts them in the job word after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker looks after a building such as a school or block of flats, the role of a janitor.

clue.text: Husband's beer-drinking volume cut by 50%

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband, as in genealogy

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the beer word contains the volume letter

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A husband's beer consumption has been halved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts V inside ALE to make ALVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to reduce it to half its size, a fifty per cent reduction.

clue.text: Champions ahead in game's final minutes

indicators.note: the word for ahead is placed inside the game word

parts.note: sport is a game; the 's is a link
a team that is up is ahead in the score

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: The champions take the lead in the closing minutes of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champions' looks like a noun but is the verb. 'in' places the word for ahead after the game word's first letter; 'final' takes the last letter of 'minutes'.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause or person is to back or support it, so champions means supports.

clue.text: Snap up German artist's "Creature of the Night"

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword shorthand for an artist
a bat is a nocturnal flying creature

explanation.surface: Buy up a German painter's work titled Creature of the Night.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab at something is to snatch eagerly at it, as when trying to snap up a bargain.
